explanation: Fires on an early subword piece of a word that is split across several tokens, mostly when the full word is easy to predict: biomedical terms (glycosamin-og-lycan, neo-ant-igen, oste-ocal-cin, triacy-lg-lycerol), 'Att' in Attorney/Attica, 'enc' in encroachment/encircling/encierro, German 'Landes-v-orsitzende'. Whole common words barely activate it.

No clear shared feature. Strong activations land on scattered tokens: 'B' in citation markers '[@B8]', subword pieces (OVH, protozoan, cirrhotic, Stratosphere, WordPress), name continuations (Merrill Lynch) and ordinary function or content words in casual prose (does, especially, your, get, continuing).

Reflexive 'self' markers: English 'self' as a compound prefix (self-titled, self-hosted, self-identifies) and the Romance reflexive clitic 'se'/'s'' (Portuguese/Spanish/French 'se propôs', 's'agrandit') fire strongly. Python 'self' arguments are moderate, and English reflexive pronouns (himself, myself, themselves) are weak.

Fires mainly on suffix or continuation pieces that complete a multi-token word or fixed phrase, often in technical or legal text: basophil-ic, scintill-ators, muscar-inic, Leptos-pires, Ord-ained, surface-mount, 'Certiorari granted', 'trails Mexico by', 'worse than expected', 'ballots cast'. Also some 'the'/'of' inside fixed phrases. The common thread is weak and the examples are mixed.

Fires on words that introduce or join items in an inclusive range or list: 'diverse as', 'businesses of all sizes', '(both X and Y)', 'both large and small', 'and'/'or' before the last item of a list, '(including', '(particularly', 'not least'. Strongest on 'as'/'both'/'all' that open a range. Plain list 'and' is moderate.

No clear concept. Top examples mix code tokens ('System[.Collections]' in C# using lines, TeX '^^M', C++ '<<', shell variable pieces), place and title names (Orient Express, Aleppo, Lubbock), and ordinary prepositions or particles in prose (along, up on, into, when).

Mainly fires on 'or' in paired alternatives or comparatives ('superior or comparable', 'same or higher', 'little or no', 'with or without', '> or =', 'rarely or never'). Also fires strongly on digits inside numbers, times and versions ('one (1) game', '+0000', '23:55', 'Interstate 265') and on some name tokens, so it does more than one job.

Fires on the noun completing a noun phrase, often a subword ending or head noun in names, political groups and objects: 'harboring a fugitive', Sandpip-ers, al Qaeda, Kurdish fighters, rebels, Young Democrats, playground, sculpture, Damon Knight. Activations are fairly low and the topics vary. This is a loose head-noun or entity-completion feature.

Verbs of transfer or handing something over to another party (share, pass, give, send, sell, rent out, deed, yield control, lend, turn over), and their particles or partitive 'of' ('pass this data on', 'give too much of', 'trade some of'). Strongest when the verb means transferring information, property or control to someone else.

The preposition 'of' right after a noun naming a part, property, aspect or component of something ('imperfections of', 'end portion of', 'set method of the Calendar class', 'components of LibreOffice', 'result of'). 'of' after quantity or purpose nouns ('the effect of', 'compare the ability of') and other prepositions are weaker.

Spatial words for sides, surfaces and relative position on an object or place (opposite, corners, upper/lower, outer/inner, surface, side, south/southern, front, bottom, ventral, circumferentially), especially in patent or technical descriptions. Also fires on the Russian equivalents.

Fires on verbs and particles in casual phrasal or idiomatic verb phrases, often motion or result ('pop it in the oven', 'turned out', 'head on over', 'sit down', 'go to work', 'from location to location', 'cope'). There are also scattered hits on 'or', commas, 'central' and 'more particularly', so the picture is noisy.

Fires on a mid- or late-word subword piece inside a long, often technical or capitalized word split into several tokens: monon-uclear, cyanoac-ry-late, tetra-hydro-biopterin, sarcoplasmic retic-ulum, MEM-OR-ANDUM, SHO-ES, HON-EST-Y, DTD, phosph-or, dip-stick. Whole common words fire weakly.

Fires on an item inside a list or coordinated noun phrase, often a category label or policy domain: 'programs for retirement, disability', 'Task Force on Immigration Policy', 'walnuts, almonds', 'size, weight or power', 'handling and storage', organization names like 'National Rifle Association'. Typically this is the first content word of a list element after a comma or 'for'/'on'.

Tech company, platform and product brand names (Windows, OnePlus, Sony, LG, Apple, Unity, Lotus, Epic Games, PlayStation), plus 'The' in code copyright headers ('Copyright 2016 The Go Authors'). Non-tech proper nouns are weak.

No coherent pattern. Top hits include the preposition 'in' in various frames ('explain their album in', 'expressed in a closed form'), subword pieces of names (Molot, Phantoms, Aldebaran), Japanese 'を', French 'la', and code tokens.

Focusing or limiting adverbs that add an emphasized qualification, chiefly 'especially' and 'particularly' (often after a comma, before 'when'/'if'/'in'), plus 'not even', 'at least' and 'not technically'. The word right after them fires only weakly.

No clear concept. Top hits mix 'be' in the GPL boilerplate 'will be useful', list 'and', Spanish 'en', PHP '<?', subword pieces of medical terms (polycythemia, megalocytosis) and of place names (Trichur, Nauvoo, Creighton), and digits.

Fires most strongly on 'links' in the Wikipedia section header 'External links' after 'References'. It also fires on tokens in other formulaic web or boilerplate phrases (cookie banner 'close this message', 'Content-type', 'did not receive a copy', 'choose the plan'). Scattered numeric and code hits are weaker.

Unclear. Fires on the modifier at the start of a compound or set phrase ('science fiction', 'science centres', 'heat-resistant', 'self-care', 'Self-Service', 'medical conditions'). It also fires on assorted punctuation and conjunctions inside fixed names (Electric & Power, 'Northern and Southern', 'aerospace, defence') and on decimal points in percentages.

Fires in list-like and proper-name contexts such as place lists, gazetteer and legal-citation text, on the separator or connector between names (commas and 'and' in lists of villages, 'village of', 'parish of', 'licensed to', 'the family Tortricidae', '(' before a year). It also fires on quote marks in JS string tables. The common thread is a delimiter right before an upcoming proper name.
